# Milestone M1: one-arm bench kit in two steps (generated by `python -m rnd.m1_kit`)

**Step 1 (one joint: GIM protocol + safety chain): $1,206 + 15% = $1,387.** **Step 2 (the rest of the arm, today's plan): $1,103 + 15% = $1,268.** Whole kit $2,656 with contingency (the previous list: $1,945, with a 10 A supply, no safety-board logic, a motors-only hold A and none of the C1/M1/M7 fix parts).

| Scenario (with contingency) | Step 2 | Whole kit |
|---|---|---|
| **Today's plan**: GIM6010 at pitch + elbow, approved inline roll | $1,268 | **$2,656** |
| Hold A yes (D20, with its drive parts) + inline roll | $1,380 | $2,767 |
| Fallback: belt roll (hold B no), GIM6010 at pitch + elbow | $1,110 | $2,498 |

Hold A (D20) costs **+$112** against the GIM6010 lines (up to +$339 at the dearest motor listing); the inline roll +$158 against the belt roll (up to +$235). Step 1: 9 of 22 lines priced from retailer snapshots, 13 ESTIMATE. Everything except the two supplies, the stand, the test lever and the catch is reused in the arm and the robot.

**Why two steps (Fable review 2026-11-27, verdict):** no GIM can be commanded until its CAN protocol is known, the arm mixes three SteadyWin drivers (docs/sw/gim_protocol_notes.md), and the arm CAD has fixes to land before printing (C1 insert pull-out, C3 rear cap, M1 inline boss/stops, M5 belt centres). Step 1 settles the protocol and the safety chain on one real GIM with only one GIM bought; the bench supply and the safety board are most of its cost and any arm needs them; Step 2 is bought when its exit criteria are met ([M1_READINESS.md](M1_READINESS.md)). **No extra GIM6010s in Step 1.**

**What Step 1 proves on hardware:** the SDC104's CAN protocol (`python -m sw.gim_discover`: MIT / impedance mode or not), enable, zero-gain and impedance control, the drive's torque limit in flash and its CAN timeout; the safety board (pre-charge, one-shot discharge, clamp, contactor, watchdog at 25 ms, e-stop → no torque ≤ 50 ms) with a real drive; torque constant and friction on a lever bolted to the output; the collision trip on one joint; the motor case temperature rise at rated torque on the lever; insert pull-out, the bolted-flange and the D50 Oldham-tongue coupons.

**Step-1 exit criterion added 2026-11-27 (software track: determinism, the Asimov sim2real lessons): soak test.** `python -m sw.soak --joints yaw,wpitch --hours 2` on the Step-1 rig. A sysid fit at the start (bring-up step `sysid`, sw/sysid.py: Coulomb + viscous friction, effective torque constant, backlash, command → response latency → sw/config/actuators_<serial>.yaml), then 2 h of 0.25 Hz cyclic motion at ≈ 50 % rated torque (2 kg at the 0.3 m lever end on the yaw stage, 0.5 kg at the wrist), then the sysid fit again with the drives hot. **Pass:** Coulomb drift ≤ 20 %, viscous ≤ 25 %, torque constant ≤ 5 %, backlash growth ≤ 0.1°, latency mean ≤ +0.5 ms and p95 ≤ +2 ms; no supervisor stop, no CAN bus-off, no new Pi throttle / under-voltage flag (`vcgencmd get_throttled`), zero implausible (corrupted) CAN frames, loop jitter p99 < 1 ms, CPU < 80 °C (rehearsed on the virtual bench: a stable drive passes, a drive whose friction drifts with temperature fails; docs/sw/sim2real_bench.md). The lever measurements of the torque constant and friction above are this step. **Proposed Step-1 line (lead to add in rnd/m1_kit.py):** one Waveshare 2-CH CAN FD HAT ($46.99) to measure SPI-CAN (MCP2518FD) against the two gs_usb adapters on the same bus ([can_interface_note.md](sw/can_interface_note.md)).

**What Step 2 proves:** the whole arm: belts and the D13 v3 stages, the bolted cartridges, the balancer (A9), the inline roll, hand sag (R2b) and, if the encoder mounts and node firmware exist by then (Fable M3), hand accuracy; the fin-ray grasp; CAN timing (SW1).

**Delta: +$137 before contingency, +$158 with it** (at the dearest motor listing +$235). The CAD and checks for both drives are in the tree (`PIP_ROLL_DRIVE=inline`, roll_inline.md). Inline-specific risks (Fable M1): the output boss joint is carried by its dowels (1.6× stall), the stops must be steel, and the 36:1 planetary adds ≈ 15 arcmin of backlash (accuracy.md: 4.3 mm at the hand without joint encoders). The SDC303 is a different driver from the Step-1 SDC104: protocol discovery runs again on it on arrival.

**Step 2, today's plan (common + hold A *no* + hold B *yes*): $1,103 + 15% = $1,268.**

Which driver version of the GIM8108-8 (SDC104, GDZ468, GDS68?) do you ship, and is it specified for 24 V? Please give rated torque, rated speed, no-load speed and continuous current at 24 V (listings quote 48 V). Price and lead time for 2 now (4 later).
2. **GIM8108-8 drawing:** installation drawing with frame diameter and height, output-flange bolt pattern (hole count, PCD, thread, depth) and housing / rear mounting pattern, and the connector position.
3. **GIM8108-36 (SDC303, 24 V):** which face is the output; the output flange material and the dowel-hole depth; reducer **backlash** (listings say 15 arcmin: measured how?); frame and connector position (we have the Ø96 × 57 drawing).
4. **GIM8108-36 output bearing:** bearing type and allowable radial load at the output flange: we need **≈ 280 N radial** continuous, with a second support bearing 68 mm behind the flange; also the allowable axial load and tilting moment (one listing gives 1000 N radial / 250 N axial: please confirm and say where it is measured). Price with the SDC303 driver and lead time.
5. **CAN protocol manual** for the SDC104 (GIM6010-8), SDC303 (GIM8108-36) and the GIM8108-8's driver: frame formats; is the MIT / impedance mode (position, velocity, kp, kd, torque feed-forward) the default or selected in the tool, and its float ranges; how to set the node ID and the feedback ID; 1 Mbit/s; a **CAN-command timeout** (the drive disables itself when commands stop) and its unit; a torque / current-limit parameter **saved to flash**; encoder zero (is the output angle kept over a power cycle?); status and error codes; under/over-voltage behaviour. **Is it the same protocol on all three drivers?**
6. **GIM6010-8:** confirm the unit is the 24 V **SDC104** version (not a 48 V listing), with its installation drawing and which face carries the housing mounting holes (rear or output face: our cartridge cap depends on it, Fable C3).

Ask Damiao (or the DM-J4310 reseller) separately: the V1.1 output bearing's allowable radial load and moment.

## What changed since the loop-47 list

- **Neon review #2 finding 15 (2026-11-27):** Step 1 no longer buys the D40 Oldham, plain Ø12 rod, set-screw pulley, 315 belt and stage bearings (belts.md: D40 disc 0.86×, plain clamp hub 0.65× at the 11 N·m peak; the yaw centre uses 93 % of its adjuster) nor the CNC rear cap (seller question 6 is open) nor the two STS3215 + USB-TTL (the only 12 V in Step 1 would have been the safety board's 1 A logic buck): the GIM is tested on a lever bolted to its output, one keyed D50 Oldham stays for the tongue coupon, and the keyed yaw stage, the cap and the servos are Step 2 lines. The safety board follows netlist v3 (Neon #2 F1: NH-50 + freewheel diodes, TLV3202, K1 hold on AUX, 60 A main fuse) and is ordered after its schematic review.
- **Two steps (Fable verdict):** Step 1 is one GIM6010-8, the DM-J4310, the two STS3215, the CAN adapters, the bench supply, the whole safety board, one D13 stage on a test lever, thermistors + one aluminium cap, inserts / screws for the coupons and filament (trimmed by Neon #2 F15, first item). Everything else waits for Step 1's exit criteria. The "zero-regret 3 extra GIM6010s" advice is gone.
- **Bench supply (M2):** Mean Well SE-1000-24 (41.7 A) for the arm's 14.8 A sustained / 31.5 A peak; the 10 A CC supply stays for the 1 A first power-up; fuses 40 A main, 20 A arm lead.
- **Safety board (M2):** netlist + block diagram in electrical.md; the forced discharge is a one-shot on the contactor's opening edge (it fought the pre-charge); 3 clamp resistors; logic parts, bleeder and a dummy load are new lines.
- **Hold A (M6):** Ø50 Oldhams, a Ø15 keyed stage, 25 mm belts, 61902 bearings and Ø96 caps are in the *yes* list (ESTIMATE until the cartridge track's D20 list), so the D20 delta is no longer motors only.
- **Inline roll (M1):** studs + nuts on the rear mount and hardened stop pins in the *yes* list; C1 tie-rod hardware, the 6061 yaw flange and the 7075 balancer crank in Step 2; 608-class balancer pulleys (M8).
- **Thermal (M7):** NTC thermistors from day 1 and an aluminium finned rear cap per GIM cartridge (thermal.md: a closed ASA sleeve allows 0.65 × rated continuous).

## Check before paying / on arrival

- GIM6010-8: the **24 V SDC104** version; DM-J4310-2EC: **V1.1** (ask for the output bearing's radial / moment rating: the wrist pitch sees ≈ 0.9 N·m bending, more with the basket hook); STS3215: the **12 V C018**.
- SE-1000-24: the 24 V model (not -12 / -48); check the overload mode on its datasheet (constant-current limiting) and set 24.0–25.2 V.
- Aluminium HTD 5M pulleys (Step 2): 15 mm belt, **12 H7 bore with a 4 mm keyway**, set screw on the key.
- Oldham coupling: **D50, 12 mm clamp-style hub with a 4 mm keyway**, OD ≤ the D50 nose bore (cartridge_m MOTOR['nose']); measure the disc (thickness, slot width and depth) and set `OLDHAM` in rnd/parts/cartridge_m.py before printing the tongue adapters.
- Vishay NH-50 (not RH-50) for the three clamp resistors: the part number starts NH050; the pre-charge and dummy-load resistors stay RH-50.
- Heat-set inserts: the short M4 (5.7 mm) the flange calls for; the long 8.1 mm ones don't fit the 6 mm flange.

**Order of work:** build and test the safety board (electrical.md, bench tests before any motor) → protocol discovery on the GIM6010-8 → bring-up on the Step-1 rig (`--joints yaw,wpitch`) → coupons (insert pull-out, bolted flange + Oldham tongue: [COUPONS.md](COUPONS.md)) → Step 2. Readiness and the go / no-go per step: [M1_READINESS.md](M1_READINESS.md). Buying is the owner's decision.
